standard_prerequisites.name: Derivability predicate
standard_prerequisites.statement: The property Deriv(x), holding when x is the Godel number of a correct natural deduction derivation, is primitive recursive; the unit proves this as its own proposition.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the first conjunct of the displayed definition of Prf_Gamma (1689-1690).

standard_prerequisites.name: End formula and open assumptions
standard_prerequisites.statement: EndFmla(x) returns the Godel number of the end formula of the derivation coded by x, and OpenAssum(z, x) says z codes an undischarged assumption of that derivation; both are primitive recursive.
standard_prerequisites.use: They tie the derivation to the sentence y and make the side condition a bounded universal over z < x (1689-1699).

standard_prerequisites.name: Primitive recursive axiom sets
standard_prerequisites.statement: Membership in Gamma is decided by a primitive recursive predicate R_Gamma.
standard_prerequisites.use: The bounded universal requires every open assumption z to satisfy R_Gamma (1686-1688, 1691-1699).

core_obligations: Fix the primitive recursive predicate R_Gamma deciding membership in Gamma (1686-1688).
Define Prf_Gamma(x, y) as Deriv(x) and EndFmla(x) = y and, for every z < x, if z codes an open assumption of x then R_Gamma(z) (1689-1699).
Each conjunct is primitive recursive and bounded quantification over z < x preserves primitivity, so Prf_Gamma is primitive recursive (1689-1699).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the primitive recursive membership predicate of Gamma.
Define Prf_Gamma from Deriv, EndFmla, OpenAssum and R_Gamma with a bounded universal, and conclude primitivity.

difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the author proposition at source lines 1679-1684: for a primitive recursive set of sentences Gamma, the relation Prf_Gamma(x, y) saying that x codes a natural deduction derivation of the sentence with Godel number y whose undischarged assumptions all lie in Gamma is primitive recursive. The author proof (1686-1700) assembles it from the unit's derivability predicate Deriv, the end-formula and open-assumption functions, the primitive recursive membership predicate R_Gamma, and bounded quantification over subderivations; writing the definition and checking that every ingredient is primitive recursive in the right sense is the counted work, with the derivability predicate delegated to the unit's own lemma.
